text.tspan: 1. The Mathematics of the Torus bleakst
A torus in Euclidean 3-space is defined by two radii:
R — the major radius (distance from the centre of the hole
to the centre of the tube)
r — the minor radius (radius of the tube itself)
This is the canonical Euclidean parametric form.
(x² + y² + z² + R² − r²)² = 4 R² (x² + y²)
This is the donut equation in implicit form.
2. The Mathematics of the Two bleakst red-blue Paths
Blue Path: a smooth parametric curve lying on the torus surface.
Red Path: a twisting helix wrapping around the tube.
Both curves satisfy the torus surface equation
because they use the same parametric embedding.
